name: Self-Directed Queries Complexity of Blockwise-Addressing
proof: Example 2 first queries $z$, which determines whether the target is an $f_i$ or a $g_i$. It then queries the corresponding private coordinates while predicting 0; the unique positive coordinate identifies the target. At most one mistake occurs at $z$ and at most one afterwards, so $\mathrm{SDC}\le2$.
